svg.text: Article · A short history of the bicycle
The first bicycle-like machine was built in Germany in 1817. It had two wheels but no
pedals, and riders pushed themselves along with their feet.
In the 1860s, pedals were added to the front wheel, but the ride was so uncomfortable
that people called the machine a "boneshaker". In the 1870s, a bicycle with a huge
front wheel became popular among young men, although it was dangerous because falling
from it could cause serious injuries.
The modern type of bicycle, with a chain and two wheels of equal size, appeared in the
1880s and was much safer. Soon after that, rubber tyres filled with air made cycling
Thanks to these changes, bicycles became cheap enough for ordinary people, and by 1900
millions of them were being used around the world.
